title: Lane Runner
observed_goal: In the frames, the observable goal is to continue moving forward along a multi-lane route, preserve the squad, and pass threats. The page presents it as an endless run; an ending, win, or loss was not observed in the frames.
observed_controls: The page instructs the player to use Drag or A/D and the left/right directions for steering.
The page lists Q for grenade, E for medkit, P for pause, and M for mute; use and responsiveness of these keys were not confirmed in the frames.
The recorded input sequence includes Enter, Space, ArrowUp, w, ArrowRight, and simultaneously holding ArrowRight + Space; a frame change alone does not establish that these inputs were accepted.
observed_core_loop: In the active frames, a squad moves forward along the route; distance reaches 54, 87, and 109 meters from 16, threat increases, enemies appear on the route, and in one frame the text says the squad fires automatically. Combo rises from 0 to 5 and the HUD coin count reaches 5. This evidence shows active gameplay and progress, but the complete and repeatable gameplay loop was not observed.
progress_feedback: The HUD directly displays squad, weapon, distance, sector, threat, combo, coins, and a progress/threat bar. The frames show numerical changes in distance, threat, combo, and coins; attributing the changes solely to the test inputs is not certain.
decisions_risk_reward: The frame after starting shows two choices, +4 soldiers and ×2 squad size, and the next frame displays text about lane selection and the difference between blue/red gates; these are stated or displayed options and risks/rewards, but successful selection, the precise effect of each option, and the consequence of a collision were not confirmed in this recording.
rewards: The frames show the HUD squad increasing from 4 to 8, combo reaching 5, and 5 visible coins. The page text also says that everything in the game is earned; the causal relationship between each increase and a specific input or event was not observed.
penalties_failure: The page/frames imply or state the existence of threats, damaging red gates, and obstacles, but damage, a reduction in squad, failure, or the end of a run was not observed in the frames.
outcomes_replay: A replay mode or direct result, win, loss, game over, or recorded result of a complete run was not observed; therefore it is unknown.
onboarding: The opening frame shows a PLAY button and a HOW TO PLAY section. After entering the game, in-frame guidance about Drag/A/D, gates, and automatic firing is visible; however, the complete tutorial path and confirmation that the controls were learned were not observed.
visual_audio_accessibility: The frames show a 3D environment with a central route, squad, enemies, obstacles, prominent HUD, and short text messages. The page has an M option for mute. The actual audio status, subtitles, other accessibility settings, readability for everyone, and audio performance were not observed.
technical_clues: A canvas with dimensions 1280×800 is recorded in the metadata; this is only a technical clue about the display surface.
The metadata records 7 scripts, 11 images, 1 stylesheet, 142 fetches, and 1 xhr, but the scripts were not scanned; game logic or configuration values cannot be inferred from these numbers.
The AudioContext warning indicates that starting audio without a user gesture was not permitted; this is a technical clue and does not establish the quality or presence of game audio.
A WebGL software fallback warning is recorded; this may affect rendering, but it does not establish the cause of frame changes or input acceptance.
No engine marker or tuning constant candidate was recorded in the metadata, and no page error or request failure was reported; several 403/400 errors and a remote config error were also recorded.
transferable_principles: Provide simultaneous feedback on continuous progress using several simple, readable indicators, without making game comprehension dependent on narrative details or specific assets.
Provide brief in-run guidance precisely when a decision is needed, and keep the distance between route selection and an observable consequence short.
In endless-run games, a gradual increase in pressure and visible counters can clarify the decision-making rhythm; the effect of each factor should be assessed with a separate test.
Keep the primary controls limited and explicit, and provide feedback for each input that can be distinguished from animation alone.
candle_climber_relevance: For Candle Climber, continuous distance/threat feedback and a gradual increase in pressure can provide abstract inspiration, but score/rank should reflect skill only.

Every reward or upgrade should provide an advantage without a purchase or wallet; the text of this game discusses earn in play, but this is only a comparative principle, not a recommendation to copy details.

An understandable linear route and limited choices could be a test idea; free brake, horizontal direction changes, or a branching route requiring new controls should not be added except as hypotheses requiring a separate test.
do_not_copy: Do not reproduce this game's name, characters, art, environment, text, sounds, brands, or assets.
Do not cite the official card's claim about survivor squad, gates, hordes, traps, and endless run as confirmed fact without an independent playthrough.
Do not conclude from a change across two frames or its simultaneity with inputs that a key or control was accepted.
Do not treat the absence of an element in the opening frame as evidence of its absence from the entire game, and do not fill in an unobserved result/loss.

evidence.claim: The opening frame shows the PLAY, DAILY RUN, ARMORY, and SETTINGS menu items and the initial score/distance/coins indicators.
In the frame after starting, active gameplay is visible with squad equal to 4, distance equal to 16m, sector 1, Drag/A/D guidance, and two choices, +4 soldiers and ×2 squad size.
In the after_key_burst frame, squad equal to 8, distance equal to 54m, and threat equal to 1.1 are visible, and the text concerns blue/red gates and lane selection.
In the after_combined_input frame, enemies are on the route, combo equals 5, distance equals 87m, 5 coins are visible, and the text “Your squad fires automatically” appears.
In the late frame, distance equals 109m, sector 1, threat equals 1.2, and squad equals 8 are visible; no result or failure is visible.
The page announces controls Drag/A/D, Q, E, P, and M, and describes the game as endless/free and without ads/paywalls/timers.
The official game card describes it as an endless run involving guiding a survivor squad, gates, hordes, and traps; this claim was not completed in this playtest.
The metadata records a frame change but explicitly warns that screenshot changes may result from animation or the passage of time and do not establish input acceptance.
The metadata records a canvas with dimensions 1280×800, an AudioContext warning, and a WebGL software fallback; these are technical clues, not proof of game logic.

limitations: This analysis is based only on evidence.json and five current frames of this game; no web browsing or fresh execution was performed. The inputs were recorded generically and start_action is none; temporal changes/animation may have played a role in the frames. The complete loop, successful gate/lane selection, effect of Q/E, audio, failure, win, replay, and final result were not observed.
